steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: Attention all residents of Zeruertza. It's a fine day.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: The results of Master Edge's survey have just been made available.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: The active Originium vein is set to explode in approximately 25 days.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: Zeruertza is officially entering the preparatory phase of evacuation, commencing now.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: Following discussions between your representatives, a general meeting will be held at a suitable timeslot in the forum.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: At that time, we will discuss the specifics of our evacuation program, as well as the dressing of our doomed city.

steps.name: Broadcast
steps.text: Residents of Zeruertza, stay tuned for further broadcasts.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Deculture. Wake up, Deculture.

steps.name: A Sleeping Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: ...good boy, Robot Stitch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: ...Deculture. Deculture.

steps.name: A Sleeping Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: You're so silly, Robot Catch.

steps.name: A Sleeping Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Let's have the both of you fight.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: What in all of love are you dreaming about?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: DECULTURE! WAKE UP!

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Hmnuh? Whazzwha?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: You know... I'd like to ask why you're taking a nap in Stitch's garden again.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Because it's so peaceful here.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: You must have missed the broadcast as well, seeing how cold you were out.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Did something happen?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Master Edge went to the other shore, did his survey, and found an Originium vein got shifted close to the tunnel entrance by the earthquake from before, and it's shockingly active too.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: We're going to hold a general meeting, and decide on how we take refuge.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: You didn't come here just to tell me that, though, did you?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: ...Right.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I'm looking for Stitch.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: If you want Stitch, I think he's ridden the boat I lent him to the other shore, to meet Master Edge and the others.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Really? I'll wait for him here, then.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Do you need him for something?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Yes. I'm hoping... he'll return to the design department and work with us in amending the dome plans.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Since Zeruertza's facing destruction, there's no sense in holding the landmark competition anymore, but we're lucky to still have some time.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: So, we'll have to make a decision at the meeting regarding how to handle that hole the earthquake left in the dome.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: I dunno, just leaving it sounds fine to me. Thoughts?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Even if we wanted to, we'd need the citizens to approve that first.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: It's an extremely significant thing to any architectural designer, letting a city reach perfection during its final moments.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: We're giving the city a final round of observation, and putting out a plan we can fulfil in the finite time we have.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: So, you're hoping Stitch will return.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I don't know why Master Finch left, all of a sudden. Others might believe their tutor-apprentice relationship was fading, or their time was just up, but I know that can't be the case.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: As a former assistant to Master Finch, I know more than anyone that despite his personal utter lack of inhibition, he cared very much for Stitch, from the bottom of his heart.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Stitch was like a son to him.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: So his departure has to have some inextricable link to Stitch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: And as industrial representative, you've seen the state Stitch has fallen into since his teacher left.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: His planning proposals kept getting overruled to the point he's slowly stopped showing up at the design department, and I've been seeing it happen and wanting to help him somehow, but I've never been able to find a way.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: This dome was left to the city as the grandest work of Stitch's teacher, Master Finch.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: But do you think, to Stitch, it might instead be a burden?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Even so, you don't want him left with any regrets, right?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: This is our last chance, Deculture.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: How very you.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Stitch, Stitch! Are you there?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Huh? What are you two doing here?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Catch! So you and Deculture got something going on, huh?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: No we don't.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Wow, ice-cold.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Keep me out of your banter, Elysium.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Master Edge, Miss Gavial, good work.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: I'm just napping here, and he's waiting for Stitch to come back.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: You're saying Stitch hasn't?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Didn't he bring you and your friends the equipment? And he made kind of a whole scene about it.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: But he vanished partway, and we don't know where he went, and here it turns out he's not home.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Tomimi ran into the runt, and said he looked pretty damned unhappy.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Any ideas?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: I... don't know.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: ...I might.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Zumama. Zumama. Not in this row, either.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Okay, move onto the next.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Ugh, this is tiring me out, a little.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I can't believe we still haven't found it.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Go on, take a break.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: About my earlier question—I'd still like to know why, Zumama.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I can't imagine you've been blind to how fine life is among the Durins.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: There's no noble conspiracies, no scheming and jockeying—and even if there is, it's just plain adorable.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Even as we're on the verge of calamity, the Durins have sufficient contingency plans in place, and they even have the leisure at this moment to consider—

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: How Zeruertza can greet its destruction in the best condition they can imagine.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I'm not denying any of that, Avdotya.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I think you're pretty on point. Durin life's not bad.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I'm not refusing you because I think what you're saying is wrong, it's because... I don't like it.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If there was a Tiacauh who wanted to come live underground, then I wouldn't stop them, and neither would Inam.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But why? I'm not just rejecting surface life out of my own experiences.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I've thought over this countless times, spending my days in the Durin cities.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I believe, and results show, the Durins live an undoubtedly better life, one more in pursuit of culture.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But why would you, or Gavial, or anyone not want a better life?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: My master isn't just wildly proficient with machines. She's really into movies, and dramas too.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: She gets me watching all sorts of stuff, and she doesn't even care if I'm interested—she explains it all to me. I've ended up remembering a few things, over time.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: For example, when she sees a character about to go on a long speech, she always says—

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: 'Ugh, long-winded righteous guys like this either turn out as villains, or they just get in the protag's way. Can't they just make their characters a little cuter...?'

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Why do you need to convince me, or Gavial?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Oh, and might I add, young lady, your view of the Durins is actually quite wide of the mark.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: In what way?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: If you'd said life in the Durin city-states was more 'on-demand,' or 'cozier,' or 'safer' of a life, I wouldn't retort.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: But you hold that the Durin lifestyle is a 'better' life, and dare I say, that alone may well be wrong.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: You're a clever child. I'm sure the distinction there doesn't fly past you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Good sir... I—I'm calling you that for now. I understand what you mean.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: But can you really say it's wrong for me to wish for others to live a more materially, spiritually plentiful life?

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: That's a different question. You're simply looking to redeem a little of the prestige you lost in an argument that's long since ended, no?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: So basically, you think the pressure to Stitch's mind, so he chose to run?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Exactly.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: And if so, my bet is he's gone to a hut by the lakeside.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Before he moved into this building, that was where he and his teacher lived together.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Catch, you know what I want to say here, don't you?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: If we end up deciding to amend the dome design, and Stitch is still unwilling, then it's down to me, right?

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: It's not just for the sake of dressing the city. From a realistic standpoint, reinforcing the dome'll buy us more time to evacuate.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: Finch and I were good friends, and I couldn't make sense of him leaving without a word either, so I'd been wanting to look after his student as best I could.

steps.name: Edge Eartheart
steps.text: There's a boundary to everything.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Miss Gavial... can we trouble you to go find Stitch?

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You didn't need to ask—I was gonna. Tomimi volunteered to help the city people out with stuff, and having an empty plate bugged me.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: I think him and I have a little debt to settle at this point, too.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Then I'll leave it to you.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: Where's that hut?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Just on the lakeside, similar style to this building. Very unique. You'll see it the moment you get there.

steps.name: Gavial
steps.text: You got it.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Catch, aren't you gonna go?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I... I don't know how I should face Stitch, under these circumstances.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But you're worried sick for him, aren't you?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Ever since Master Finch vanished, I've been wanting to help him, but I just don't know how.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: C'mon. Do I diagnose you with 'too nice,' or 'way way way too nice?'

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Nah, I guess you Durins do give me that kind of vibe, on the whole.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: For reasons I don't know either, Stitch actually has kind of an inferiority thing.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: With his type of personality? You greet him with what you think is an equal approach, but to him, it actually comes off like a sort of pressure from on high.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Because for him, it takes everything he's got just to pretend he's on the same level as you guys.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You can't just invest some sincerity and expect results when it comes to communicating.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: So, what should I do?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Well, alright. You treat me like a brother, in times like these, I'll teach you a thing or two, just how brothers should.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: It's actually real simple. You don't say anything like 'I want a fair competition with you,' and you don't say to him, 'you've got a choice.'

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: You seal off his escape route, and you tell him, 'you've got no choice, but I'll be right there with you, and we'll do our best.'

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: A man who spends too long shut in his own self-made space tends to need a little prodding, from time to time.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Miss Deculture, what do you say?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Why ask me?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I'm just making some of my own guesses here, but you, you clearly know him better than anyone.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Stitch does have a sort of inferiority complex.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: You might just be right. He doesn't need tender comfort, he needs someone to really yank him out.

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Won't that... hurt him?

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: It will, and it's not guaranteed to turn out pretty.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: But if this is his last chance, as you say—

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Then you ask yourself too, do you just want to get along better with him, or do you want him to make his way out, even if it makes your relationship worse?

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: I'll give it a try.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Then I think you oughta speed it up.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Or we get Gavial's fists instead, and those sure don't settle for 'yank him out.'

steps.name: Catch Lightrace
steps.text: Haha, I'll get going now, then!

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Lively, extroverted, grasps social contact. They're all fine character traits, Catch.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: You believe people should become that way, and you do work to see that happen.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: But you can't always hope for everyone else to be like you.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Elysium's right too, and if I'm going to help Stitch, maybe that's what I need to do.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: But I think distress and evasion are just as correct, too.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Catch, seeing as you're going to do things your way, I'll do things my way.

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: If Stitch wants to run, I'll help him run.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Deculture. Deculture. Do you need us?

steps.name: Deculture Silvermint
steps.text: Go. Help Stitch out.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: If Miss Deculture wasn't doing it on purpose, then she doesn't realize just how easy it actually is to read her face.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: She doesn't agree with what I say at all, heheh.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Man—I haven't felt this youthful a vibe in forever. It makes me wanna join in on the fun a little.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Nah. If I did go, I might just get swept in by Gavial.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: I don't want to be beaten for no good reason.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Okay, Stitch! You'd better shake up and wake up.

steps.name: Elysium
steps.text: Turn a blind eye to all these guys who want to help you, and you don't know how it might come back to haunt you.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I don't understand. You people clearly aren't as unreasonable as Gavial.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Why do you insist so much on—

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Indulging her?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I ask you, do you not look at Gavial and feel that we need someone like her?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Inam, weren't you waiting outside?

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: You spent so long in here, I thought you were up to something...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Avdotya, you and I happen to be similar in ways.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: A huge part of why I came to serve as Acahualla's Messenger was that I wanted to escape the unending strife between the lords ameer.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Acahualla has nothing to speak of, but life here is extremely comfortable. I'm a big fan of this land.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: And also, if we're raising worries, then I'm more worried than you about the Durins' showing up causing issues.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Then why are you still...

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Gavial's been gone from Acahualla for so many years, and hasn't changed one bit.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: As if nothing, anywhere, across all the four corners could make her surrender.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: When I see Gavial, I think to myself, 'ah—so people like you still exist.'

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: I can't help but want to help her.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: It's that simple.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Before I left Acahualla with Gavial, I was completely ignorant.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I've seen so many things with Rhodes Island, but I've slowly realized that what I'm really learning isn't just knowledge.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: There's so much across the world that I've never thought of, that at the same time is exactly how you should expect.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I'm sure Gavial's seen plenty where she's just as powerless too.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: My dream is to build the mightiest machine in any land.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: But truth is, I still haven't figured out what I should use it for when I'm done.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Still, seeing Gavial, I've gradually gotten some sort of idea.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: The machines I make will be used to help her.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: There'll come a day when Gavial's fists meet a wall they can't break through.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: But that's not a problem with her. She's flesh and blood too, after all.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And just like I've done here and now, I'll give her the greatest weapon.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: If fists won't do it, then take an axe. If an axe won't do it, then take a hammer. If a hammer won't do it, then take a drill. If a drill won't do it, then I'll build her an entire Big, Ugly Thing.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And if a Big Ugly won't do it, then I'll build her a nomadic city, and whatever she wants to do with that, she will.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: You really trust her that much?

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: I do. Because Gavial stands for Acahualla better than anyone or anything ever could.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: She's the backbone of us, and in future, she'll be the backbone of even more.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: And it's in our power, our own power, to make sure Gavial's fists are unhindered for eternity.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Of course, realistically, I'm just as worried what leaving Acahualla to her purview will result in.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: With Gavial's temperament, giving her authority might discomfort the powers more than it will her.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: So, if she really was going to serve as lord ameer, I was planning to thoroughly groom her for it for a stretch.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: It probably wouldn't have done anything.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Haha, I think so too.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: But even I never pictured I'd be willing to go so far for her.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: Your experiences have taught you to doubt people like Gavial from the start.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: I don't deny that.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: So, maybe you can try to start by believing in her.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: ...I'll give it an attempt.

steps.name: Inam
steps.text: So. The map?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Ah... I forgot.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: Oh, I see you left it to this old codger and all these bots to actually, conscientiously search, while you were all tied up arguing in Gavial's favor.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: And I only just realized this shelf has absolutely nothing to do with travel records!

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: So I went to the other side and took a look, and I found it straight away.

steps.name: High Priest
steps.text: I think it's this we want?

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Strange Machine
steps.text: Avdotya: dummy. Avdotya.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Fine... I know, I was wrong, I'm sorry!

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Is that enough?!

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Ah, Avdotya! Brilliant, you're still here.

steps.name: Croque Diamondface
steps.text: Master Edge sent a message a moment ago. He's proposing we hold that general meeting in the forum now, and the other representatives are all in favor. Now we need your view.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Thank you, Zumama.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Though I still don't entirely accept it, perhaps—I can indeed give it an attempt.

steps.name: Eunectes
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Avdotya
steps.text: Croque, tell Master Edge—I have no objections, and moreover, I'll be there to persuade the residents of Zeruertza.
